title: VLSM and efficient division of address blocks

videos.script: One block of addresses, and four networks that need it: a hundred hosts, fifty, twenty, and two. {{needs}} Cut the block into four equal pieces, and the biggest network does not fit, while the smallest wastes sixty addresses. {{fixed}} This lesson gives each network the size it needs. You will add two, round up, sort from the largest, and place each one where the last one ended. {{plan}} A calculator checks the arithmetic, and a drawing of the block shows where everything landed. {{bar}} Then the plan is built on two routers, and tested from head office. {{build}} The upstream router holds one route for all of it. You will see what that buys, and the loop it causes for an address nobody has. {{loop}} And last, one mistyped mask that makes two subnets overlap. Nothing complains on the day it is typed, and you will see why. {{overlap}} Every command runs in this course's lab, so every number on the screen is one the machines printed. {{lab}}
